messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Missing Covariate Data
parts:
On Mon, 2024-01-29 at 11:56 -0800, ethier....@gmail.com wrote:
> I have a follow up question to this FAQ:
>
> Q. Can INLA deal with missing covariates?
>
> A. No, INLA has no way to `impute' or integrate-out missing
> covariates. You have to adjust your model to account for missing
> covariates. Sometimes, you can formulate a joint model for the data
> and the covariates, but this is case-specific.
>

this is still the situation.


> (1) If we include a dataframe with missing covarites in the INLA
> model, how does INLA treat rows or columns with missing data? How
> might this effect the output (I would assume reduced power, potential
> bias).


fixed effects that are NA, are set to zero, like

x[is.na(x)] <- 0

arguments to f(), like f(idx), then the contribution from f() is removed
for which(is.na(idx))

>
> (2) If one assumes that the covariate data are missing at random, what
> is the best way to adjust a model to account for the missing
> covariates? Can they simply be removed/ ignored?


There is no clear answer to this, as it depends on its context. In any
case, nothing 'automatic' is happening in INLA, you have to do this
yourself.

>
> (3) If only a few data points aro missing, is it worth imputing?

observations, in the sense of not being used as covariates for other
data, can be left as NA, this means that there is no likelihood
contribution from these NA observations in the model.

Best
H

--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org
